name: Min Heap
description: A complete binary tree where every parent is smaller than or equal to its children. The minimum element is always at the root.
aim: Maintain a min-heap where the smallest element is always at root, supporting O(log n) insert and O(log n) extract-min.
howItWorks: Insert: add at end, bubble up (sift up) until heap property restored
Extract-min: remove root, move last element to root, sift down
Sift-down: compare with children, swap with smaller child if needed
Build heap: apply sift-down from last non-leaf to root — O(n)

complexity.spaceDescription: O(n) for heap array; insert/delete O(log n), build heap O(n)

realWorld: Priority queues — process smallest job first
Merge k sorted lists — always pick smallest next element
whenToUse: Need O(log n) insert + O(1) minimum access
Priority scheduling where smallest = highest priority
alternatives: Max-heap — when maximum needs fast access
Fibonacci heap — O(1) amortized decrease-key for Dijkstra
